## Abstract
  Early childcare has a strong equalizing potential, yet access remains socioeconomically stratified. This study examines how these socioeconomic inequalities emerge and widen across three stages of the early childcare access process: intention to use early childcare during pregnancy, application, and actual access during the child’s first year. Using longitudinal data on approximately 2,000 families in France, collected during pregnancy and followed one year after birth, we document a progressive widening of gaps along the access pathway. Compared with high–socioeconomic status (SES) households, low–SES households are 15 percentage points less likely to intend to use early childcare, 20 percentage points less likely to apply, and 31 percentage points less likely to obtain access. To identify the determinants of these gaps, we combine machine learning for variable selection with decomposition analyses that quantify the contribution of observable factors at each stage across a wide range of 40 predictors. At the intention stage, most of the SES gap is accounted for by differences in observable characteristics related to resources, constraints, and available alternatives, with norms contributing little. At subsequent stages, inequalities increasingly reflect institutional barriers. The largest disparities emerge at the access stage, where spot allocation-related factors account for most of the gap, particularly application timing, employment status, income, and knowledge of the childcare system. Overall, the results show that socioeconomic stratification in early childcare access is closely linked to the timing and design of the access processes, even in systems intended to be universal.

## How to download and replicate {#replicate}

To reproduce the findings and re-run the analysis, do the following:

1. Download and install this repository. 
2. Open `Intention.Rproj` to open an [RStudio Project](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/workflow-projects.html).
3. Within the RStudio Project, open the `Manuscrit.qmd` file and run it to replicate the figures and tables of the main paper
4. Within the RStudio Project, open the `Supplementary Materials.qmd` file and run it to replicate the figures and tables of the SI Appendix. Note that for convenience (it is much slower), Lasso and Elastic nets robustness checks are performed in another file: `Lasso_Elastic_Nets.qmd`. Same for the RF with Recursive Feature Elimination: `RFE_RFtuning_def.qmd`. Running this code is at your own discretion. It may take several days to run on a standard computer.

The source code can be found in the `.qmd` and `.R` files. 

Please find the [session info below](#session-info).

*Estimated installation time* : If you have R and Rstudio installed, then adding additional packages required in our R scripts is quick (a couple of minutes)

*Estimated run time*: Rendering the `Manuscrit.qmd` document takes about 5mins on our machine, both on Mac and PC (see [session info](#session-info))

## Files glossary {#glossary}

The `codebook.csv` contains all variables of our data set.

The `Data/` folder contains the main data sets.

- `Data/MainDB_analysis.csv` is the main data set used for the analyses. 
- `Data/Sapatial Data/txcouv_pe_com_EAJE_assmat.csv` contains data on early childcare access in France necessary for 

The `RScripts/` folder contains the scripts necessary to  that we rely upon in our analysis scripts. To keep the `Manuscrit.Rmd` document neat and readable, we wrote all lengthy code bits as external functions.

 - `RScripts/AllFunctions.R` contains all functions used in the analysis.
 - `RScripts/LoadAllData.R` contains the code to load the data.
 - `RScripts/LoadInstallPackages.R` contains the code to install and load all necessary packages.

 

`Figures/` contains the  figures used in the manuscript.

`.bib` contains all references for the manuscript and `.csl` the citation formatting.

`images/` contains images used for this ReadME file.
